subject: old toothbrush
title: What If You Never Replaced Your Toothbrush?

scenes.text: What if you never replaced your toothbrush? It would still look clean. That's the trap.
Dental associations say swap it every three to four months, because worn bristles clean less well.
Brushing twice a day, that's over 700 brushings a year, each one bending the bristles a little further out.
Between uses, a damp brush is a home for microbes. Shut it in a closed case and they grow faster.
In one university study of shared bathrooms, over half the toothbrushes carried fecal bacteria, most likely from someone else.
The twist: there's little evidence those germs make you sick. The real cost is a brush that cleans less every year.
